title: Scaling Categorical Flow Maps
gist: Apple researchers (with University of Oxford co-authors) trained a 1.7B-parameter continuous flow model on 2.1T tokens and self-distilled it into a Categorical Flow Map that produces high-quality text in as few as 4 inference steps, the first evidence that non-autoregressive flow-matching language models scale past the <1B regime. They also derive a likelihood bound that lets CFMs be scored on standard LM benchmarks, landing in the same range as discrete diffusion methods.

themes.theme: Flow matching as an autoregressive alternative

insights.claim: Continuous diffusion and flow matching models are being positioned as a viable alternative to autoregressive language modelling because they unlock capabilities reserved for continuous modalities, including accelerated sampling and tilting.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: If flow-based LMs mature, the inference-cost structure of language models changes — fewer sequential steps means less latency-bound GPU time per token, which pressures the token-per-second economics that current autoregressive serving stacks are built around.
insights.locator: Abstract opening: 'Continuous diffusion and flow matching models could represent a powerful alternative'

insights.claim: Discrete text data can be generated by a continuous process via a simple flow matching procedure between a Gaussian and the one-hot encoded data distribution, which is the mechanism that makes continuous generative modelling applicable to language.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The Gaussian-to-one-hot bridge is the reusable primitive to watch: any lab adopting it inherits the few-step sampling advantage without redesigning the tokenizer stack.
insights.quote: generating discrete data continuously by a simple flow matching process between a Gaussian and the one-hot encoded data distribution
insights.locator: Abstract: 'Recently, several works have demonstrated the possibility'

insights.claim: Prior to this work, Categorical Flow Maps had only been evaluated below roughly 1B parameters, leaving their scalability entirely unproven.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames the field's maturity: as of this paper, few-step non-autoregressive text generation was still a small-scale research curiosity, so any commercial claim built on it before now rested on untested extrapolation.
insights.quote: this method had only been evaluated at relatively modest scales (< 1B), leaving the question of its scalability completely open
insights.locator: Abstract: 'However, this method had only been evaluated'

insights.claim: A 1.7B-parameter base flow model trained on 2.1T tokens and self-distilled into a Categorical Flow Map generates diverse, high-quality text in as few as 4 inference steps while maintaining near-data-level token entropy.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Four-step generation at a 2.1T-token training budget is the concrete datapoint to benchmark against: it sets the current bar for how cheap non-autoregressive text inference can get without collapsing output diversity.
insights.quote: we train a 1.7B-parameter base flow model on 2.1T tokens and self-distill it into a CFM that generates diverse, high-quality text in as few as 4 inference steps while maintaining near-data-level token entropy
insights.locator: Abstract: 'In this article, we train a 1.7B-parameter base flow model'

insights.claim: Preserving near-data-level token entropy is treated as the key quality guardrail for few-step distilled text generation, not just sample fluency.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Entropy retention is the metric that separates a genuinely diverse fast sampler from a mode-collapsed one — worth demanding from any vendor pitching few-step text models.

insights.claim: A newly introduced likelihood bound for Categorical Flow Maps in the semi-discrete setting allows these models to be scored on standard language-model benchmarks, where they land in the same range as discrete diffusion methods.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Comparability matters more than the headline number: once flow models can be scored on the same benchmarks as diffusion and autoregressive models, buyers can finally price the quality gap instead of guessing at it.
insights.quote: we introduce a likelihood bound for CFMs in the semi-discrete setting, and show that they can be used to score the model on standard LM benchmarks, achieving results in the same range as discrete diffusion methods
insights.locator: Abstract: 'Furthermore, we introduce a likelihood bound for CFMs'

insights.claim: Training categorical flow models at scale surfaces distinct challenges whose practical remedies lie in loss weighting and time scheduling choices.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The scaling bottleneck is recipe knowledge, not raw compute — meaning the labs that publish these prescriptions (here, Apple) keep an execution lead even when the architecture itself is public.
insights.quote: we uncover some of the challenges that arise from training these models at scale, and we provide prescriptive insights on loss weighting and time scheduling
insights.locator: Abstract closing: 'Finally, we uncover some of the challenges'
